No anonymous parcel feature response or downloadable safe parcel layer was exposed.

requestsAndEndpointChecks.outcome: HTTP 200 official OLARMS landing page. It describes Ogun State land registration, property registration, land search, allocation, and related services, but exposes no parcel schema, CRS, native parcel ID, or public geometry response.

HTTP 200 official OLARMS-GIS/GeoSense Pro informational page. It advertises dynamic layered Ogun maps including land parcels and digitized cadastral maps, and links to the GIS map and login; no public feature service URL or schema was exposed in the page.

HTTP 200 public map landing page. The current JavaScript/configuration initializes Leaflet with an OpenStreetMap basemap, Ogun bounds [6.201,2.602]-[7.990,4.702], and no parcel overlays; it then warns that full experience requires login and redirects to /gis/web_map. No parcel layer, CRS, ID field, or geometry endpoint was present.
HTTP 200 response body 'Please log in first.' Authentication wall; no login, credentials, token, CAPTCHA bypass, or private route was attempted.

HTTP 200 public frontend configuration. It exposes the public API base https://olarmsapi.ogunstate.gov.ng/api/v1/ and token-based authorization function, but no parcel endpoint or anonymous parcel data. No token was created or used.
HTTP 404 Not Found at the API root; this is not evidence of absent Ogun parcels or absent service coverage.
HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed for an unauthenticated GET; no authenticated request or unsafe record lookup was attempted.

HTTP 200 federal informational pages describing national cadastral/legal survey responsibilities and map/coordinate/cadastral survey requests. General federal agency prose, not city/local public parcel-service evidence for Ago-Iwoye.
